items.title: Multiplicativity of the determinant of a (2,1)-periodic complex under the factorization of one of the three endomorphisms
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Under the two kernel/image hypotheses I_alpha = K_{beta gamma} and K_alpha = I_{beta gamma} for every permutation of the three endomorphisms alpha, beta, gamma of a finite length module M over a local ring, the lemma asserts that three triples are exact (2, 1)-periodic complexes and that det_kappa(M, alpha, beta gamma) = det_kappa(I_gamma, alpha, beta) det_kappa(M/K_beta, alpha, gamma) (statement lines 16982-17010). The exactness parts are reductions through specifically constructed short exact sequences 0 -> I_{beta gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{alpha gamma} -> 0 and 0 -> I_{alpha gamma} -> I_gamma -> I_{beta gamma} -> 0 (proof lines 17016-17030) together with the check alpha(K_beta) subset K_beta, gamma(K_beta) subset K_beta computed as alpha(I_{gamma alpha}) = I_{alpha gamma alpha} subset I_{alpha gamma} = K_beta (proof lines 17033-17041). The determinant identity itself is not a computation with the definition: the author chooses admissible sequences x, y, z generating K_alpha, K_beta, K_gamma together with lifts x-tilde, y-tilde, z-tilde, records the length bookkeeping length_R(I_alpha) = s + t, length_R(I_beta) = r + t, length_R(I_gamma) = r + s and length_R(M) = r + s + t, then characterizes each of the three determinants as the unique scalar in kappa^* in a displayed relation between two symbols and multiplies the three relations, keeping track of the signs (-1)^{r(s+t)}, (-1)^{rt} and (-1)^{rs} (proof lines 17044-17103). The construction of the admissible sequences and the sign bookkeeping are the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
